notes: Test questions T1-T12 from runs/ai-analyst-how-much-context-research.md section 7, worded exactly as asked, so mark_run.py can match them by id and text. Batch 1 (before the new note) and batch 2 (after) each ask T1-T12.

Chat plan: every test question is its own fresh chat; there are no follow-ups, so no row has follow_up_of. T5-T12 are Repeats of T1-T4 (same wording, definition and family); their rivals are the T1-T4 rival rows in the same family. The truth is the same in both batches: every answer is marked against the definition the new note writes down.

The truth follows the new note approved by Saurabh on 31 October 2026 (PLAN.md, Piece 3), not piece 2's spec, on missing delivery dates: delivered orders with no order_delivered_customer_date are left out of both the late count (T1) and the late-share denominator (T2). Why: the note under test defines it that way, and the truth has to mark answers against the definition the team wrote down. Piece 2's reading (missing dates kept in the denominator as not late) is rival T2c; the gap between T2 and T2c is display rounding at one decimal, not a finding (rule 12). For T1 the count is the same either way, since an order with no delivery date can't be late.

'Delivered in <year>' is read as order_status = 'delivered' in the <year> purchase cohort (order_purchase_timestamp), as the metrics note and the new note define it. Delivery-date rivals (T1c, T1d, T2e, T2f, T3b, T3d, T4b) read the year from order_delivered_customer_date; T3b is the reading piece 2's chats gave for item price (context only, rule 4).

'Late' is calendar-day grain: the date part of order_delivered_customer_date later than the date part of order_estimated_delivery_date. Timestamp-grain rivals (T1b, T1d, T2b, T2d, T2f) also count orders delivered on the estimated day as late.

Item price (T3) is price only, freight excluded. Freight rivals (T3c, T3d, T3f) and all-status rivals (T3e, T3f) are added. Summing price per order then across orders equals the plain sum of price, so one formula serves. The payments table is not loaded in Dot's workspace, so payment_value has no row.
Rows with asked: false are computed but not asked. Date filters use string prefixes on the raw CSV text; every value is computed from the raw CSVs. reviewed_by is left for a person to set.

Restructured 31 October 2026, before review and before the run: T13-T24 removed. stage_gate.py treats a batch as complete only when it has an entry for every asked row, so both batches ask T1-T12 and are told apart by batch number. No definition or value changed.
